insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Plan-dependent (Base Sum Insured options shown: 5/7.5/10/15/20/25/50/75/100/200 Lakhs depending on plan)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be At Actuals unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: Room rent is payable at actuals unless a different limit is mentioned in your Policy Schedule. This reduces the risk of room-rent linked deductions in hospital bills.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Secure Benefit becomes available only after your Base Sum Insured is fully exhausted. This gives extra coverage once your main sum insured runs out.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.reference: Section B.2.6 (Automatic Restore Benefit), point vi, page 18
great.explanation: Restored sum insured can be used even for the same illness within the same policy year. This helps if you need repeat hospitalizations for a recurring condition.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.reference: Section B.2.4 (Plus Benefit), point c, page 16
great.explanation: Plus Benefit applies irrespective of the number of claims in the expiring policy. This means the benefit does not get forfeited just because you made a claim.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 180 days after discharge (unless the Policy Schedule says otherwise). This supports follow-up treatment like medicines and diagnostics after hospitalization.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage (unless the Policy Schedule specifies otherwise). Claims for declared/known conditions during this period can be rejected.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.reference: Section C.1.b (Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period), page 28
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This delays coverage for those named treatments even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the policy start date, except for accidents. Early claims for fever/infections etc. can be denied during this period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 60 days before admission (unless the Policy Schedule says otherwise). This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred by the Insured Person during the Policy Year towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance (airplane/helicopter) expenses are covered during the policy year. This can be valuable for critical transfers, but may be subject to limits/terms in the policy or schedule.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred during the Policy Year on Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization expenses are covered when treatment is taken at home as per policy conditions. This helps when hospital admission is not possible or medically not advised.

good.name: Home Health Care
good.quote: This Cover is not available on reimbursement basis.
good.explanation: Home Health Care is not available on a reimbursement basis. You may need to use the insurer's cashless/arranged service, otherwise you may not be able to claim it.

good.name: Deductible
good.quote: The Insured Person shall bear an amount equal to the Aggregate Deductible specified on Policy Schedule once in a Policy Year post which coverage shall commence under this policy
good.explanation: An aggregate deductible (as per Policy Schedule) must be paid once in a policy year before the cover starts paying. This increases your out-of-pocket cost upfront but can reduce premium.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as food charges (other than patients diet provided by hospital), laundry charges, attendant charges... Full list of Non-Medical Expenses is attached as ANNEXURE B
bad.reference: Section C.3.k (Specific Exclusions) & Annexure B, pages 32 and 49-50
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed in Annexure B (e.g., attendant, laundry, food charges etc.) are excluded. This can materially increase out-of-pocket expenses during hospitalization.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
